predecessors.name: Kingdom of Serbia (1718-1739)
predecessors.text: the Habsburg Kingdom of Serbia (1718-1739), ceded back to the Ottomans in the Treaty of Belgrade of 1739

successors.name: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)
successors.text: the Principality of Serbia: "The Second Serbian Uprising, led by Miloš Obrenović, produced a semi-independent Principality of Serbia" in 1817

ledger.x: 1739: the Treaty of Belgrade ends the Austro-Turkish War of 1737-1739 and the Habsburg Kingdom of Serbia; "1739-1817: Rumelia Eyalet (nominally until 1830), with the Ottomans reconquering the sanjak".
8 October 1789: Belgrade falls to Austria in the Austro-Turkish War of 1787-1791.
1793: Kladovo is added to the pashalik; the page gives the span 1793-1801 and does not say from which Ottoman province.
February 1804: the Dahije slaughter the Serb knezes and the First Serbian Uprising begins.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1813: the First Serbian Uprising is suppressed; Derendeli Ali Pasha and then Sulejman Pasha Skopljak (1813-1815) govern.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1815: the page gives no start for the Second Serbian Uprising and dates only its success to 1817; the year is bridged from the pasha list (Marashli Ali Pasha, 1815-1817) and the 1814 Hadži Prodan revolt.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1817: the Second Serbian Uprising, led by Miloš Obrenović, "produced a semi-independent Principality of Serbia".
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1817: the page ends the sanjak with the creation of the Principality of Serbia; a ferman of Mahmud II confirmed it in 1830.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1787-1791
wars.outcome: Austria besieged Belgrade from 15 September to 8 October 1789 and held it until the Treaty of Sistova in 1791 returned it to the Ottomans.

wars.name: First Serbian Uprising
wars.outcome: Sparked by the slaughter of the knezes on 4 February 1804; suppressed in 1813.

wars.name: Second Serbian Uprising
wars.outcome: Led by Miloš Obrenović; produced a semi-independent Principality of Serbia in 1817.

certainty.note: An Ottoman province with no surveyed frontier; the page gives no nahiye list, so the extent is a reading of central Serbia.
